drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 defines Foundry as an autonomous computational-systems factory whose purpose is to convert intent into verified running systems and keep actual systems aligned with intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01's founding thesis states that implementation artifacts are replaceable while the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, and verification obligations is the durable asset Foundry preserves.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §2 reports frozen 9K/9L discovery coverage identical to a frontier baseline (31/32 critical, 55/58 overall), which the design treats as the reason not to reframe discovery.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v1

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §1.2 states v1 finds the right unresolved issues then emits each several times under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §3.1 and §4.3 assign open-ended meaning to AI proposals and state mutation to deterministic Foundry admission; EV-T3-01 implements that only AdmissionRoute.APPLY may change semantic state.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §5–6 selects Option C: ephemeral SemanticIssueCandidates from unchanged discovery, AI cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation into persistent semantic state, then late classification and gap projection.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 marks the same design PROPOSED and not approved; EV-T2-01 marks locked core architecture with core-slice implementation authorised. Both speak to this design's approval state.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §23.1 locks single-pass cleanliness as a subsystem gate and longitudinal T1–T6 reconciliation, including model/agent takeover, as the primary validation target.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §7.2 and EV-T3-02 make address_id the only identity; subject, facet, and scope are versioned descriptors Foundry never compares for equality to decide sameness.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §7.2.1 and §12 lock non-destructive equivalence: both addresses and claims remain, a representative view is derived, and EV-T3-01 appends an EquivalenceRecord without copying or moving claims.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §7.3 and EV-T3-02 state that claims are immutable assertions that are never merged, rewritten, or averaged.
drafts.subject: SemanticClaim

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §9 [9N LOCK] restricts implemented core-slice relations to EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, and CONFLICTS_WITH, treating binding and supersession as judgment operations rather than ontology relations.
drafts.subject: Semantic relations

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §8 and §13 treat incompatibility as admitted claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH that deterministically yields DISPUTED, which consolidation cannot clear and only authority can settle.
drafts.subject: Semantic conflict

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §3 and §17 remove GapKind from identity and assign it after consolidation by AI over the consolidated issue.
drafts.subject: GapKind

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §17 states a Gap is a deterministic projection from persistent semantic state, not the durable record; the durable object is the issue at an address.
drafts.subject: Gap

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §4.5 and EV-T3-02 make address equality a current-interpretation referential fact only after an admitted binding, ending on supersession; EV-T3-01 refuses a second bind of an actively bound candidate until that judgment is superseded.
drafts.subject: Candidate binding

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §20.1 locks risk-based routes APPLY, REQUIRE_SECOND_LENS, REQUIRE_HUMAN, and REJECT, and forbids confidence or recency from conferring semantic authority.
drafts.subject: Admission

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §19.1 requires a generic DERIVED_FROM primitive so superseding an admitted semantic basis marks transitive descendants stale in the current view without rewriting historical records.
drafts.subject: Supersession

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §1.1 locks that the pipeline starts from any project evidence rather than typed human requirements, with greenfield and brownfield converging on one semantic substrate.
drafts.subject: Intent Engine

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §17.1 locks that closure is always evaluated for a scope and is never assumed globally.
drafts.subject: Closure

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 §25.1 defines a versioned, scoped Intent-to-Decision handoff carrying semantic-state revision, representative addresses, claims, conflicts, provenance, authority, stale dependencies, and scoped closure by stable ID.
drafts.subject: Intent-Decision handoff

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 and EV-T2-01 state the v1 defect as duplicate emission of the same issues without durable identity or governed consolidation.

value.text: v1 discovers the right unresolved issues but emits each one several times under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage between discovery and emission

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 4.5 locks referential identity as a current-interpretation fact that ends on supersession; EV-T3-01 and EV-T3-02 implement that a candidate stays bound until that judgment is superseded.

value.text: After Foundry admits that candidate X refers to ADDR-x, address equality is a deterministic referential fact only under the current admitted interpretation; it is not a new semantic inference, not eternal truth, and it ends when that binding judgment is superseded

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 section 4.5 treats an admitted binding as making sameness at ADDR-x deterministic and authoritative, without the later current-interpretation limit.

value.text: After AI binds a candidate to ADDR-x and Foundry admits that binding, the statement that two issues at ADDR-x are about the same thing becomes deterministic and authoritative

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 19.1 requires DERIVED_FROM blast-radius propagation; EV-T3-01 records derivation edges and supersession records while leaving targets readable.

value.text: a generic append-only DERIVED_FROM primitive so that superseding an admitted semantic basis marks every transitive descendant STALE/NEEDS_RECONCILIATION in the current view without rewriting historical records

drafts.rationale: Both design revisions say Gap is a projection from persistent issues, not the durable object.

value.text: projected view, not a durable record; the durable object is the semantic issue at an address

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 status header states the design is proposed, not approved, and not implemented.

value.text: PROPOSED — awaiting architect review; not approved; not implemented

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 status header states locked core architecture with architect approval and authorised core-slice implementation.

value.text: LOCKED CORE ARCHITECTURE — architect-approved; core-slice implementation authorised

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 20.1 specifies those four admission routes and forbids confidence or last-writer rules as authority.

value.text: risk-based APPLY, REQUIRE_SECOND_LENS, REQUIRE_HUMAN, or REJECT; confidence and recency never confer authority

drafts.rationale: Design section 7.2 and EV-T3-02 state that only address_id is identity and that descriptor equality must not decide sameness.

value.text: only address_id identifies a SemanticAddress; subject, facet and scope are versioned descriptors and are never equality keys

drafts.rationale: Both design revisions recommend Option C and reject gap-centric consolidation and semantic-state-first discovery for v2's first form.

value.text: Option C — hybrid: SemanticIssueCandidate discovery, then governed persistent state, then gap projection

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 opening purpose statement defines Foundry as converting intent into verified running systems and keeping actual state aligned.

value.text: to convert intent into verified running systems and continuously keep actual systems aligned with their intended state

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 9 locks the 9N core-slice relation vocabulary to those three values; EV-T3-01 implements those relation proposals.

value.text: EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, CONFLICTS_WITH

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 section 9 lists seven relation values as the v2 vocabulary, including NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, and OVERLAPS.

value.text: EQUIVALENT, NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, CONFLICTS_WITH, OVERLAPS, DISTINCT

drafts.rationale: Both design revisions report the frozen 9K/9L discovery figures as identical coverage, not a Foundry-only win.

value.text: critical 31/32 and overall 55/58, identical to the frontier baseline concept for concept

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 founding thesis names that decision system as the durable asset and treats code and other artifacts as replaceable.

value.text: the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, contracts, invariants, rationale, authority, and verification obligations; implementation artifacts are replaceable

drafts.rationale: Both design revisions state this AI-propose / Foundry-apply boundary as the contract every later section must obey.

value.text: AI may propose a state-changing semantic judgment but never apply one; deterministic Foundry may apply or refuse a transition but never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 sections 7.2.1 and 12 lock non-destructive equivalence; EV-T3-01 appends EquivalenceRecord without copying claims and EV-T3-02 forbids destructive merge.

value.text: non-destructive: both addresses, claims, evidence edges and historical references are retained; an admitted EQUIVALENT judgment derives a reversible representative current view

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 sections 9 and 12 define EQUIVALENT as merging addresses while leaving claims unmerged.

value.text: EQUIVALENT is the only merge-eligible relation and it merges addresses, not claims

drafts.rationale: Both design revisions and EV-T3-02 define SemanticClaim as immutable and never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

value.text: append-only; never merged, rewritten, or averaged

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 25.1 specifies that Intent-to-Decision handoff payload and that 9N defines the contract without implementing its consumer.

value.text: versioned and scoped; for one scope it carries semantic-state revision, representative addresses, claims, conflicts, provenance, authority, relevant supersession, stale-dependency blast radius, and scoped closure, pointing to durable IDs rather than duplicating the ledger

drafts.rationale: Both designs treat conflict as first-class DISPUTED state from claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH; EV-T3-01 records ConflictRecord without merging claim values.

value.text: multiple claims at one address plus an admitted CONFLICTS_WITH relation yield DISPUTED; claims are never merged and consolidation cannot clear DISPUTED

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 1.1 locks the Intent Engine entry point as any project evidence rather than typed human requirements.

value.text: any project evidence via one ingestion contract; human-written requirements are one source among many; greenfield and brownfield converge on the same semantic substrate

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 23.1 locks single-pass metrics as a subsystem gate and longitudinal T1–T6 as the primary validation target.

value.text: single-pass cleanliness is a subsystem quality gate; primary validation is longitudinal T1–T6 reconciliation across evidence, conflict, authority, blast radius, and model succession

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 section 23 states the primary testable claim as those single-pass metrics against a one-shot baseline.

value.text: primary testable claim is single-pass: preserve critical recall, strictly improve useful precision and redundancy/unsupported rates, and maintain safety versus a one-shot baseline

drafts.rationale: EV-T2-01 section 17.1 locks closure as scoped evaluation, allowing one scope to proceed while another remains blocked.

value.text: always evaluated per scope and never assumed globally

drafts.rationale: Both design revisions assign GapKind after consolidation and remove it from identity because v1 duplicates never shared a kind.

value.text: assigned by AI after consolidation over the consolidated issue; removed from identity entirely
